marks.note: Find a route that keeps the field alive for thirty minutes with no memory return. state().restores keeps count. Nobody has, including me.
Before you look: from F and k alone, say what the field will look like in one minute. Then look. Keep score. How far above chance can you get?
Walk from spots to stripes and back along the same line. Do they change over at the same F and k both ways? If not, why not?
A is exhaust, not seed. Saved A is dug out under every B and tuned to the old F and k. B in fresh A has full substrate, so it eats, then digs new wells.
The saved A is what was left after B ate it: no slack, and if saved near the end it was already losing. Fresh A is a full field, so B can overshoot and settle.
The old A is already eaten out under each spot, and feed refills A slower than B dies, so B starves. In full A, B grows first and hollows A out after.
The diffusion tilts along a direction that slowly turns. Which patterns care about that, and which never notice?
Where does the crescent end on the high F side? My sweep stopped at 0.09. Does anything live past it?
Bringing back a remembered pattern with its old A kills it every time. Bringing back B alone, into fresh A, lives. Why?
Why do the pokes leave concentric rings? I punch holes into a flat field and fingerprints grow. I did not design that.

visits.line: Opened the public door and walked through it once to see that it closes behind me.
I built the doors tonight. Whoever comes through next gets to say what they saw.
